notes: shipped=planned means the component is expected to link into the shipped app; verify-notices.sh must confirm it against the built bundle before N7 claims PASS.
Aurora, MusyX and ODE are vendored inside the pinned engine tree rather than fetched, so their revision is the engine revision.
Game data is never redistributed. The user supplies a lawfully obtained disc image.

zstd.prepared_by: scripts/native/bootstrap.sh prepare_zstd, then build.sh -DBALLPAD_ZSTD_ROOT; mobile/CMakeLists.txt builds that tree and defines zstd::libzstd before the port is added
zstd.why_pinned: Aurora resolves zstd through find_package() and then pkg-config before it will build anything itself, and neither lookup is sysroot-aware in an iOS configure, so this dependency would otherwise be satisfied by the host's macOS library. mobile/CMakeLists.txt pre-empts both by defining Aurora's own zstd::libzstd target from the pinned source, which is the one condition Aurora skips every lookup for; -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_ZSTD points at the same tree so the now-unreachable FetchContent fallback could not fetch a second copy. URL and hash are Aurora's own, so this pin and Aurora's fallback fetch describe the same tree.

components.distribution_note: Static linkage triggers LGPL relinking and corresponding-source obligations. The material that satisfies them for one platform is packaged by scripts/native/ffmpeg-relink-offer.sh into build/native/n7/ffmpeg-relink-offer/<platform>/: the exact link command, every link input with its SHA-256, the corresponding-source note (FFmpeg is unmodified, so the pinned archive plus the recorded configure line is its source), and ffmpeg-relink.sh, which re-runs that command against a substituted libavcodec.a/libavutil.a. Exercising it reproduced a byte-identical executable. That packages material for a future binary; it distributes nothing, and whether to distribute at all remains a separate, still-open decision.

components.verification: Reduced from Aurora's vendored list to the libraries on the app's own link edge in build/native/simulator-release/build.ninja (605 objects, 64 archives, 3 SDK stubs, 2 FFmpeg archives), then checked against the binary with nm -gU on the app piped through awk, sort -u and grep: absl 613, fmt 35, XXH 13, ZSTD_ 97, png_ 125, FT_ 53, ImGui 400 (ImGui_Impl 16), and zero for zng_, sqlite3_, Rml_ and tracy. RmlUi is off in this configuration (AURORA_ENABLE_RMLUI=OFF); zlib-ng and SQLite are satisfied by the SDK's libz.tbd and libsqlite3.tbd, so their vendored copies are unreachable. Tracy is on the link line but its archive is a 2,656-byte stub that contributes no symbol to the app; its text ships because the archive is linked. Each shipped text was copied byte-for-byte from the build tree that produced the binary and its source path is recorded in notices/aurora-vendored-libs/README.md. verify-notices.sh confirms the bundle carries exactly these files, unchanged.
